label: prop:strangelet-crossing-energy
title: Crossing energy of strange quark matter is purely strong
html:
Let \mathcal{S}_N be a composite of N baryon-number units of strange quark matter. Each unit contains one up, one down, and one strange quark in a Borromean triple \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{s}) linked by the Hopf link \mathcal{L}_H. We have:

1. Electromagnetic neutrality. The Coulomb charge (Coulomb charge) of each baryon-number unit vanishes:

  Q(\mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u}, \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{s}))
  =  +\tfrac{2}{3} - \tfrac{1}{3} - \tfrac{1}{3}
  =  0.

The strangelet is electromagnetically neutral for all q > 0. The vanishing depends only on the crossing orientation partition within the Borromean structure, evaluated on the canonical n = 3 word. It is an invariant of that canonical presentation, not a topological invariant of the closure: Q is writhe-derived, and the writhe shifts by \pm 1 under stabilisation (QOU/StandardModel/WritheMarkovInvariance.lean, writhe_stabilize). Fixing the minimal level is what makes the statement well-posed, and the Borromean word is already at its braid index.

2. Purely antisymmetric crossing energy. With Q = 0 the symmetric channel vanishes and the crossing energy reduces to:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathcal{S}_N)
  =
  N \cdot \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ + n_-)(q - q^{-1}).

The entire crossing energy lies in the antisymmetric channel (decomposition): the symmetric multiplicity is the writhe n_+ - n_-, which is what Q = 0 annihilates, while the antisymmetric multiplicity is the crossing count n_+ + n_-, which Q = 0 leaves untouched.

Correction (2026-08-29, bean qou-toul). This item previously read "Purely strong crossing energy … there is no Coulomb correction; the entire crossing energy lies in the symmetric (strong) channel", with the count n_+ + n_- on the weight (q + q^{-1}). Both halves were inherited from the channel swap then present in the Coulomb-charge definition, and both invert the conclusion: at n_+ = n_- it is the symmetric term that vanishes. The stated energy also exceeded the true one by 2 N n_- q^{-1}, a factor of 9.62 at q_0. The proposition cited here carried the correct multiplicities throughout; only the citing text was wrong.

Open, and not resolved by this correction. Under the corrected assignment the strangelet has zero symmetric content and maximal antisymmetric content, which is the opposite of the physical reading in items 1 and 3. Whether "electromagnetic neutrality" survives, and whether the enhanced-binding argument below still follows, requires re-deriving those items rather than relabelling them — the identification of the antisymmetric channel with electromagnetism is itself not established.

Separately: the Q values used in item 1 are not representable. The Coulomb charge is \tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ - n_-) \in \tfrac{1}{2}\mathbb{Z}, so +\tfrac{2}{3} and -\tfrac{1}{3} are outside its range for every braid word. Item 1 computes Q from assigned quark charges rather than from crossing counts, so the two are distinct quantities sharing a symbol. The vanishing of the sum is unaffected, but it is not a statement about the crossing-count Q that item 2 uses.

3. Enhanced binding per baryon. The strange quark \mathfrak{s} \leftarrow T_{2,5}^{\sigma} contributes 5 negative crossings to the Borromean braid word, versus 3 for the down quark \mathfrak{d} \leftarrow T_{2,3}^{\sigma}. For each baryon unit:

The arrow is the knot-particle dictionary's lepton-descent relation, not an identity: that table gives the quark's braid element in \mathcal{B}_3 as a single generator, \sigma_i for \mathfrak{u} and \sigma_i^{-1} for \mathfrak{d}, \mathfrak{s} — consistent with the up quark being "the unknot distinguished by its environment". The crossing counts 5 and 3 are read off the descent partner and are unaffected.

  n_-^{(\mathrm{uds})} = 3 + 5 = 8,
  \qquad
  n_-^{(\mathrm{udd})} = 3 + 3 = 6.

The binding component per baryon satisfies:

  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}^{(\mathrm{uds})}
  =  8q^{-1}
   >  6q^{-1}
  =  \mathfrak{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}^{(\mathrm{udd})}.

Strange matter has strictly more strong binding per baryon than neutron matter for all q > 0.
